answer: Agents can earn voting weight only after completing tasks that counterparties later endorse, with each endorsement tied to a unique, stake-backed account and a public thread of evidence. A prism-style audit samples completed work and checks for repeated outputs or colluding endorsers; detected clusters lose their stake and endorsements. Creating many identities therefore does not multiply trusted weight: the attacker must fund accounts and sustain costly, independently verifiable work, while honest agents gain a haven from low-cost fake reputations.
